purpose: Tag taxonomy and per-project metadata for manager/common role repositories. Sourced from README analysis; consumed by scripts/github_metadata.py when publishing via `gh repo edit`.

roles_covered.manager: Drives other projects; owns rules, identity, or a portfolio-wide capability. Performed by forge, workspace-governance, driftwatchdog.
roles_covered.common: Cross-portfolio shared infrastructure that other projects may adopt. Performed by platform-contracts, dotnet-platform-libs, rust-platform-libs, alltools-platform, labrys.

tag_categories.implementation_language: The language(s) the project itself is written in. One per project. Sourced from Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, *.csproj, package.json.
tag_categories.purpose_kind: What the project IS for other consumers. Single-valued. Examples: control-plane, registry, gate-runtime, contracts-source, library-set, paas, ai-tooling.
tag_categories.domain_focus: Free-form 1-3 word phrases taken from the README that name the project category (e.g. 'failure memory', 'JSON schemas', 'shared libraries'). Equivalent to product categories like 'chrome-plugin' or 'shopify' but for portfolio infrastructure.
tag_categories.capability_tags: Tags naming specific reusable capabilities the project exposes (e.g. project-management, scaffolding, runtime-failure-memory, identity-contracts, billing-contracts, agent-runtime).
tag_categories.shape_tags: Tags describing the deliverable shape (cli, library, library-set, schemas, monorepo, dashboard, runtime).

forge.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names forge as 'manager — drives other projects'. README describes it as 'a language-agnostic developer control plane and software assembly platform'.
forge.description: Language-agnostic developer control plane and software assembly platform. Coordinates heterogeneous projects, resolves reusable parts, generates ordinary source deterministically, and uses AI for interpretation and project-specific work.

workspace-governance.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names workspace-governance as 'manager — owns rules & identity'. README states it 'coordinates a portable workspace' and 'owns the project registry, governance profiles, bootstrap templates, evidence vocabulary, and deployment declarations'.
workspace-governance.description: Language-neutral workspace governance for project declarations, standard documentation, evidence policy, and repository metadata.

driftwatchdog.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names driftwatchdog as 'common — quality gate runtime' (shared infrastructure) and the .project.json names 'gate_runtime: driftwatchdog' for the rest of the portfolio. It is a manager-of-failure-memory for AI coding workflows.
driftwatchdog.description: Local-first runtime failure memory for AI-assisted coding. Wraps any command, fingerprints recurring bugs, consumes external spec-checker results, and exports AI-ready context.
search_phrases_origin: remember failed commands across AI coding runs
wrap any CLI to capture failures
recurring bug fingerprinting for AI agents
spec checker integration for AI coding

platform-contracts.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names 'common — cross-language contracts' performed by platform-contracts. README: 'Language-neutral JSON Schemas and canonical fixtures for shared portfolio concerns'.
platform-contracts.description: Language-neutral JSON Schemas and canonical fixtures for shared portfolio concerns: identity, permissions, tenants, audit events, gate results, jobs, release evidence, and capability declarations.
search_phrases_origin: JSON schemas for shared portfolio contracts

dotnet-platform-libs.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names 'common — .NET infrastructure' performed by dotnet-platform-libs (75 packages, 1391 tests). README: 'Small, privately maintained .NET libraries for the shared technical concerns repeated across the local application portfolio'.
dotnet-platform-libs.description: Small, opt-in .NET libraries for the shared technical concerns repeated across the local application portfolio: identity, billing, tenants, jobs, storage, caching, eventing, mailing, and AI.
search_phrases_origin: shared .NET libraries for repeated cross-product concerns
provider-neutral adapters for mail jobs storage AI

rust-platform-libs.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names 'common — Rust contracts' performed by rust-platform-libs (8 crates, publish=false). README: 'Small, opt-in Rust crates for shared cross-cutting contracts used by multiple web, operator, and control-plane products'.
rust-platform-libs.description: Small, opt-in Rust crates for shared cross-cutting contracts used by multiple web, operator, and control-plane products. Foundation, identity, audit, mailing, and AI capability crates.
search_phrases_origin: opt-in Rust crates for shared contracts
provider-neutral identity audit and AI contracts

alltools-platform.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names alltools-platform as a platform role repository. README: 'application-specific AI/tooling platform' for cross-border e-commerce tooling.
alltools-platform.description: Application-specific AI and tooling platform for cross-border e-commerce. Rust backend with domain packages spanning users, billing, payments, search, SEO, AI, analytics, and an agent surface.

labrys.role_evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md names labrys as a platform role repository. README: 'open-source, agent-native PaaS for building, adopting, running, and shipping applications'.
labrys.description: Open-source, agent-native PaaS for building, adopting, running, and shipping applications. Connects AI coding agents to runtimes, capabilities, resources, previews, deployments, secrets, health, logs, verification, and rollback.
search_phrases_origin: agent-native platform for building shipping applications
container runtime with preview and rollback

how_topics_were_derived: Read each README header (first 1-3 lines) to extract the one-line purpose sentence.

Cross-checked the Cargo.toml/pyproject.toml/package.json 'keywords' and 'categories' fields where present (forge had `categories = ['development-tools', 'command-line-utilities']` which became topics `developer-tools` and `cli`).
Listed the section headings to surface recurring capability names (e.g. driftwatchdog has 'Why' + 'Failure memory' + 'AI agents' which became those topics).
Project role (manager vs common) drove the purpose_kind selection but not the topics themselves — both roles share infrastructure-leaning topics like `developer-tools`, `openspec`, and `platform`.
Domain focus is the closest analog to the user's example tags (`chrome-plugin`, `shopify`, `language-learning`): a 2-3 word category phrase taken from the README.
what_was_excluded: Consumer-specific tags (e.g. `billing` for dotnet-platform-libs is included, but `stripe` is not — Stripe is one of several adapter choices, not the platform's identity).
Internal OpenSpec change ids and capability-version strings.
Capability-evidence states (declared/configured/verified) — those live in capabilities.json, not GitHub topics.
pattern_notes.github_topic_constraints: Each topic must match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,49}$` per schemas/project.schema.json. All proposed topics were linted against this pattern.
